data.name: GoNNER
data.detailed_description:
E é assim, bem de repente, que atualizamos nosso primeiro jogo premiado pela IGF! GoNNER BlüEBERRY EdiTION adiciona novas armas, cabeças, tipos de inimigos e um novo desafio, e ainda novos visuais doces como só eles! E sim, também tem mirtilos na história.

Volte aos pulos para GoNNER se faz tempo que não joga! E se perder a cabeça por isso, tudo bem — temos muito mais de onde essa veio.

Subitamente, fizemos uma atualização no nosso primeiro jogo vencedor dos IGF! GoNNER BlüEBERRY EdiTION adiciona novas armas, cabeças, tipos de inimigos e um novo desafio, assim como uns quantos visuais sensacionais. E claro, não podiam faltar os mirtilos.

Já faz muito tempo, volta a jogar o GoNNER! E mesmo que percas a cabeça, há muitas mais para usares.

GoNNER é um jogo de plataformas geradas aleatoriamente baseado na pontuação com elementos roguelike e uma dificuldade de fazer arrepiar. GoNNER é ainda uma história de amizade entre Ikk, a Morte, e uma baleia espacial chamada Sally.

Vais morrer. Muitas vezes. O estilo do jogo é mesmo esse, mas ele não é injusto. Com o tempo vais encontrar o jeito de GoNNER, por isso não percas a cabeça. Mas se a perderes, não há problema, temos um monte de cabeças substitutas para usares.



- DESAFIOS DIÁRIOS! Jogáveis apenas uma vez por dia. Os níveis são gerados aleatoriamente, mas neste modo todos jogam no mesmo mundo e usam equipamentos idênticos. Tudo é redefinido à meia-noite (horário da Suécia). Conseguirás esmagar os adversários na tabela de classificações?

- GERADO DE MODO ALEATÓRIO! Cada vez que jogares os mundos serão diferentes, oferecendo desafios e oportunidades ímpares.

- DESBLOQUEÁVEIS! Podes escolher entre várias habilidades passivas e ativas no início de cada sequência, por isso lembra-te de experimentá-las todas até encontrares a mais adequada ao teu estilo.

- SEGREDOS! Existem áreas secretas no mundo de GoNNER, e elas vão dar-te itens diferentes que podem ser muito úteis no início de cada sequência. Não vamos contar-te como chegar a essas áreas, ou que critérios são necessários para as encontrar, afinal segredos são segredos.

- CLASSIFICAÇÕES! Mata criaturas, faz combos, marca pontos e gaba-te junto dos amigos da tua superioridade.

- MÚSICA! E é realmente incrível.

Boa sorte.

data.short_description: GoNNER é um jogo de plataformas em 2D geradas aleatoriamente com elementos roguelike e uma dificuldade de fazer arrepiar. Segue o bastante incompreendido e altruísta Ikk numa jornada para alegrar a sua única companhia neste mundo - uma gigantesca baleia encalhada chamada Sally - procurando a prenda ideal nos lugares mais profundos e...

reviews.review:
My Lovely Daughter is a grim management simulation and narrative-driven experience that explores grief, obsession, parental responsibility, and the disturbing consequences of treating living beings as tools. Developed by GameChanger Studio and published by Toge Productions, Neon Doctrine, and Raw Fury, it places players in the role of Faust, an alchemist who awakens without his memories and discovers that his beloved daughter has died. Rather than accepting this loss, he becomes determined to restore her soul through alchemy, beginning a cycle of experiments that grows increasingly unsettling as the true cost of resurrection becomes apparent.

The central gameplay revolves around creating homunculi, artificial daughters brought to life through alchemical experiments. These beings possess different personalities and characteristics, and Faust can interact with them while developing their abilities and emotional connections. The disturbing element comes from knowing that they were not created simply to be cared for. They ultimately serve Faust's larger objective, and progressing toward the resurrection of his real daughter requires exploiting and sacrificing them. This creates an unusual conflict between the player's instinct to become attached to individual homunculi and the mechanical necessity of treating them as expendable resources.

Management plays a significant role in this process. Homunculi can be sent to work around the town, generating money and other resources needed to continue Faust's research. The player must decide how to use each daughter efficiently while maintaining the broader cycle of experimentation. What initially resembles a relatively straightforward resource-management system becomes uncomfortable because nearly every decision reinforces the game's darker themes. The more useful or likable a particular homunculus becomes, the harder it can feel to sacrifice her, yet refusing to do so interferes with Faust's objective. The game effectively turns ordinary optimization decisions into moral compromises.

This relationship between mechanics and narrative is one of the game's greatest strengths. Instead of presenting cruelty exclusively through scripted scenes, My Lovely Daughter makes the player directly participate in Faust's actions. Repeating the process of creating, employing, developing, and sacrificing homunculi gradually risks turning these characters into statistics and resources in the player's mind. That uncomfortable normalization appears deliberate. It reflects the game's broader examination of exploitation, abusive parenting, child labor, and the way authority figures can justify cruelty when pursuing something they consider more important.

Faust himself is equally important to the experience. His desire to recover his daughter initially gives him a sympathetic motivation, but the increasingly terrible methods required to accomplish that goal complicate any straightforward interpretation of him as a grieving father. His missing memories introduce an additional mystery, encouraging players to uncover information about his past and understand the events surrounding his daughter's death. Collectible letters and other discoveries provide additional context, while multiple endings encourage further experimentation and repeated playthroughs for anyone determined to piece together the larger story.

The visual presentation complements the subject matter particularly well. Hand-drawn artwork gives the world a distinctive gothic character without relying entirely on graphic horror. Many of the homunculi have designs capable of inspiring sympathy or curiosity, which makes their intended purpose considerably more disturbing. Environments and character illustrations create a melancholy atmosphere, while the soundtrack reinforces the feeling of isolation and tragedy surrounding Faust's experiments. Horror here is largely psychological and thematic rather than dependent on constant monsters, combat, or jump scares.

There are weaknesses in the structure, particularly its reliance on repetition. The recurring process of producing homunculi, sending them to work, gathering resources, interacting with them, and conducting further experiments can eventually become predictable. Although repetition supports the narrative idea of Faust becoming trapped in an obsessive cycle, thematic justification does not completely eliminate mechanical fatigue. Players seeking an exceptionally deep economic or management simulator may also find the underlying systems less elaborate than expected. Much of the game's appeal comes from how those mechanics interact with the narrative rather than their complexity when considered independently.

Replayability is strengthened by the different homunculi, hidden information, achievements, collectible material, and multiple possible endings. Seeing everything requires more commitment than simply reaching one conclusion, and additional playthroughs can change how earlier events are interpreted. However, revisiting the repetitive management loop may not appeal equally to everyone. The game is best suited to players who value experimental storytelling and psychological discomfort more than constant mechanical variety.

Steam Deck compatibility is somewhat less straightforward than with games carrying a clearly established official Deck rating. My Lovely Daughter does not have a prominent official Steam Deck compatibility classification that guarantees a fully optimized handheld experience. Because it was originally designed around conventional PC controls and interface expectations, Deck users should consider it an unofficial or potentially configuration-dependent experience rather than assuming complete Verified-level support. Controller mapping or Steam Input adjustments may be useful, and compatibility can vary depending on the current Proton environment and game configuration.

Ultimately, My Lovely Daughter is memorable because it refuses to separate its uncomfortable story from the player's actions. The repetitive management systems occasionally work against its pacing, but they also reinforce the central idea of obsession gradually overriding compassion. Its haunting artwork, somber atmosphere, morally troubling decisions, mysterious narrative, and unusual approach to resource management create a distinctive experience that is difficult to confuse with conventional simulation or horror games. Players willing to engage with its deliberately upsetting themes will find an ambitious examination of grief and exploitation, even if its mechanical loop occasionally struggles to maintain the same strength as its storytelling.

Rating: 8/10
